title: Zero-boundary Hölder Hessian solutions from finite-mass Hölder subsolutions on strongly m-pseudoconvex domains with n/2 less than m less than n
source_title: The Hölder continuous subsolution theorem for complex Hessian equations
author: Amel Benali; Ahmed Zeriahi
difficulty_reason: The source-specific obstacle envelope and near-boundary Hessian mass comparison must establish global superlinear capacity domination, not merely quote an interior capacity estimate. The complete mixed-Hessian regularization and integration-by-parts induction converts Lebesgue L1 approximation into measure L1 control in the zero-boundary setting. The authors then combine capacitary stability, global glued approximants and the corrected stability exponent to obtain boundary Hölder regularity with the selected explicit threshold; all of that new local chain is retained.
